definition_zh: 原木；圆木；航海日志；记录簿；记录；累计达到（里程、工时）
definition_en: a thick piece of cut or fallen tree; an official written record of events on a ship or aircraft; to write down events or figures in such a record; to travel or work a stated amount that is added to a total
core_image: 斧头落下去，树干断成一截一截，木纹里还渗着树脂
scene: 码头边的空地上，卡车后挡板放下，几截树干滚了下来。A thick log rolled off the truck and landed in the mud.
sceneCN: 这里是「伐下的整段树干」（第 1 个义项：未经加工的原木）；句意为一段粗大的原木从卡车上滚下来，落进了泥地里。

pos.zh: 记录；把……记入日志；累计达到

derivatives.zh: 由 log 加表示「人」的后缀 -er 构成，义为「伐木工；记录员」
由 log 加 -ing 构成，义为「伐木作业」
由 log 与 book 复合而成，义为「日志簿；记录本」
由 back 与 log 复合而成，义为「积压未办的工作」
由 log 与 in 复合而成，义为「登录」

senses.title: A thick piece of cut tree
senses.definition: a thick piece of wood cut from a tree, or a whole trunk lying where it fell
senses.definitionCN: 从树上砍下的粗大木段，或倒在地上未经处理的整根树干
senses.example: The cabin walls were built from rough logs.
senses.exampleCN: 小木屋的墙是用粗糙的原木垒起来的。
senses.why: Middle English logge already meant a lump of wood, and this concrete sense has stayed at the centre of the word ever since.
senses.whyCN: 中古英语 logge 已经指一截木头，这个最具体的义项从中古一直留到今天，是整组词义的中心。

senses.title: An official record of a voyage or flight
senses.definition: an official written record of events kept on a ship, an aircraft or a machine
senses.definitionCN: 船、飞机或机器上保存的正式事件记录
senses.example: The captain wrote the storm into the ship's log.
senses.exampleCN: 船长把这场风暴写进了航海日志。
senses.why: Sailors measured speed by throwing a weighted piece of wood overboard and reading the line; the figures went into a book, and the book took the name of the wood.
senses.whyCN: 船员把一块系着重物的木头抛进海里测速，再读线上的刻度；数字记进本子，本子便沿用了那块木头的名字。

senses.title: To write something down in a record
senses.definition: to write an event, figure or message into an official record as it happens
senses.definitionCN: 把发生的事情、数字或消息在发生时写入正式记录
senses.example: Officers logged every radio message during the night.
senses.exampleCN: 夜里，值班人员把每一条无线电消息都记了下来。
senses.why: Once log named the book, the same word could name the act of writing in it, so the record and the recording share one form.
senses.whyCN: 当 log 指那本簿子之后，同一个词自然也能指在簿子上书写这件事，于是「记录」和「被记录的内容」共用一个形式。

senses.title: To add up distance or working time
senses.definition: to travel or work an amount that is added to a running total
senses.definitionCN: 走过的距离或工作的时间被累加进一个总数
senses.example: The old bus has logged more than a million kilometres.
senses.exampleCN: 这辆旧巴士累计跑了一百多万公里。
senses.why: A logbook keeps a running total, so the verb came to mean reaching a figure that the book will hold.
senses.whyCN: 日志簿记的是一路累加的总数，所以动词又指达到某个会被写进簿子的数字。

intro.en: Log appears in Middle English as a word for a block of wood, and its further origin is uncertain; the record sense grew out of sailors measuring speed with a wooden chip.
intro.cn: log 在中古英语里就指一截木头，更早的来源不确定；记录义则从船员用木块测速这件事上长出来。

items.en: The word is first recorded in Middle English as logge, a block of wood, and no earlier form is securely attested.
items.cn: 这个词最早见于中古英语，写作 logge，指一截木头；更早的形式没有可靠的书面证据。

items.en: Logge named a cut block or a fallen trunk, the rough timber used for walls and for firewood.
items.cn: logge 指砍下的木块或倒下的树干，就是用来垒墙和烧火的粗木料。

items.en: Some dictionaries suggest a connection with Scandinavian words for something lying down, but the link is not certain.
items.cn: 一些词典认为它与斯堪的纳维亚语中表示「躺倒之物」的词有关，但这一联系并不确定。

items.en: A weighted wooden chip was thrown overboard to measure a ship's speed, and the readings were kept in a log book.
items.cn: 人们把一块加重的小木板抛到船外测速，读数记在航海日志里。

items.en: The word extends to any systematic record, then to computer sign-ins and to totals of distance or hours.
items.cn: 词义扩展到任何系统化的记录，再进入计算机登录，也表示里程或工时的累计。

note.en: The look-alike group is built from log plus common English elements; the near-meaning group gathers words for wood and for written records.
note.cn: 形近组由 log 与常见英语成分组合而成；近义组收表示木材和书面记录的词。

entries.definition: An official book in which events are recorded.
entries.definitionCN: 记录事件的正式簿子；日志簿。

entries.definition: A person who cuts timber or keeps a record.

normalIntro.en: Log starts as a plain word for a block of wood; the written record comes from the wooden chip sailors threw into the sea.
normalIntro.cn: log 起初只是「一截木头」的朴素说法；书面记录义则来自船员抛进海里的那块木片。

normal.en: Middle English wrote logge for a cut block of wood, and that solid sense never left the word.
normal.cn: 中古英语把砍下的一截木头写作 logge，这个实在的意思一直没有离开这个词。

normal.en: Sailors threw a weighted chip into the water, read the line, and wrote the figures in a book, so the book was named after the wood.
normal.cn: 船员把加重的小木片抛进水里，读线上的刻度，再把数字写进本子，本子便跟着木头得了名。

normal.en: Logger adds -er to log: the person who cuts the timber or keeps the record.
normal.cn: logger 在 log 后加 -er：砍木头的人，或负责记记录的人。

normal.en: Logbook is log and book joined directly, a book that holds the entries.
normal.cn: logbook 是 log 与 book 直接拼在一起，指收纳这些记录的本子。

normal.en: Backlog is back plus log: entries that piled up behind the rest, now any unfinished work.
normal.cn: backlog 是 back 加 log：堆在后面的记录，如今指任何积压未办的工作。

abstract.en: A cut block and a record book share one word, which suggests English treats a countable thing and a checkable trace as close neighbours.
abstract.cn: 一截木头和一本记录簿共用一个词，说明英语把「可数的东西」和「可查的痕迹」看得很近。

abstract.en: The chip thrown overboard is a reminder that a record is built from readings someone can check, not from memory.
abstract.cn: 抛到船外的那块木片提醒人：记录靠的是一次次可以核对的读数，而不是记忆。

abstract.en: Turn the pages of a log and time is cut into lines, which is the most practical picture this word offers.
abstract.cn: 一页页翻日志，时间就被切成一行一行，这是这个词最实用的画面。

examples.en: A fallen log blocked the path through the forest.
examples.cn: 一段倒下的原木挡住了穿过森林的小路。

examples.en: The pilot logged six hours of flying time that week.
examples.cn: 那名飞行员那一周累计飞行了六个小时。

examples.en: Every visitor is logged at the front desk.
examples.cn: 每位来访者都在前台做了登记。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「烙个」——把每天的事烙在本子上，就成了日志；log 既是木头，也是记录。

root: 来源不确定：中古英语 logge 已指「砍下的木块」，一般认为可能与斯堪的纳维亚语中表示「躺倒的树」的词有关，但没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The concrete sense is a cut trunk; the record sense grew from sailors writing down what a floating chip told them, and from there the word covers any systematic account.
sensesIntro.cn: 具体的义项是砍下的树干；记录义从船员把浮木读出的数字写下来开始，再扩展到任何系统化的记载。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an axe bites into a trunk and the cut block falls away.
core.cn: 核心意象：斧头咬进树干，砍下的一截木块滚落在地。

branches.en: a captain writing by lamplight on a rolling ship

definition_zh: 对数；以某数为底求得某数所需的幂
definition_en: the power to which a fixed base must be raised to produce a given number
core_image: 一本旧数表摊开，密密麻麻的数字排成纵列，每一列都在回答「要抬到几次」
scene: 旧数表翻到发黄的一页，学生用指尖顺着纵列往下找。Before calculators, students found products by looking up a logarithm in a printed table.
sceneCN: 这里 logarithm 指「对数，即为得到某数需要把底数抬到的幂」（第 1 个义项：对数的定义）；句意为在计算器出现之前，学生通过查印刷数表里的对数来求乘积。图中可辨识物件：对数表、书页、指尖、铅笔。

senses.title: The power needed to reach a number
senses.definition: the exponent to which a base must be raised to produce a given number
senses.definitionCN: 为使底数得到某个给定数而必须把底数抬到的幂
senses.example: The logarithm answers the question of how many times the base must multiply itself.
senses.exampleCN: 对数回答的是底数必须自乘多少次这个问题。
senses.why: the word was coined from Greek logoi 'ratios' plus arithmos 'number': the ratio-number, the number that measures the ratio.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由希腊语 logoi「比」与 arithmos「数」合成：比数，即衡量比值的那个数。

senses.title: The common logarithm
senses.definition: a logarithm taken to base ten, written without an explicit base in many texts
senses.definitionCN: 以十为底的对数，许多教材中不写出底数
senses.example: The common logarithm of one thousand is three.
senses.exampleCN: 一千的常用对数是三。
senses.why: base ten matches the decimal system, so the ten-based logarithm became the everyday one in calculation.
senses.whyCN: 以十为底与十进制相合，因此十底对数成了计算中的日常对数。

senses.title: The natural logarithm
senses.definition: a logarithm taken to the natural constant, the base that makes growth and decay equations simplest
senses.definitionCN: 以自然常数为底的对数，这个底使增长与衰减的方程最简洁
senses.example: The natural logarithm turns multiplication of growth factors into addition.
senses.exampleCN: 自然对数把增长因子的相乘变成相加。
senses.why: calculus keeps choosing the base whose logarithm has the simplest slope, and that base is called natural for this reason.
senses.whyCN: 微积分总是选那个对数斜率最简单的底，这个底正因此被称为「自然」。

senses.title: The binary logarithm
senses.definition: a logarithm taken to base two, common in computing
senses.definitionCN: 以二为底的对数，常见于计算领域
senses.example: The binary logarithm of the number of leaves gives the depth of the tree.
senses.exampleCN: 叶子数量的二进制对数给出这棵树的深度。
senses.why: computer memory splits in two at every step, so base two measures its depth exactly.
senses.whyCN: 计算机存储每一步都一分为二，因此以二为底正好量出它的深度。

senses.title: A table of logarithms
senses.definition: a printed table listing logarithms so that products can be found by adding
senses.definitionCN: 印好的对数数值表，靠相加就能求出乘积
senses.example: The engineer carried a logarithm table in the same case as his slide rule.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师把对数表和计算尺装在同一个盒子里。
senses.why: before machines, the table was the practical form of the idea: turn multiplication into addition and look it up.
senses.whyCN: 在没有机器的年代，数表就是这个想法的实用形态：把乘法变成加法再查表。

senses.title: A law of logarithms
senses.definition: a rule such as the logarithm of a product equals the sum of logarithms
senses.definitionCN: 诸如「积的对数等于对数的和」这样的规则
senses.example: The law of logarithms replaced a long multiplication with two short additions.
senses.exampleCN: 对数运算法则把一次很长的乘法换成两次短加法。
senses.why: the whole reason logarithms were invented is that they turn products into sums, which is exactly what the law states.
senses.whyCN: 对数被发明的全部理由就在于把积化为和，这条法则说的正是这件事。

senses.title: The logarithm as a function
senses.definition: the function that assigns to each positive number its logarithm
senses.definitionCN: 把每个正数对应到它的对数的函数
senses.example: The logarithm grows slowly, so it compresses huge ranges into a small interval.
senses.exampleCN: 对数函数增长缓慢，把巨大的范围压进一个小间隔。
senses.why: once the numerical value became a rule applied to every positive input, the logarithm was a function.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个数值变成对每个正输入都适用的规则，对数就成了一个函数。

senses.title: The discrete logarithm
senses.definition: the exponent that solves a power equation within a finite arithmetic system, used in cryptography
senses.definitionCN: 在有限算术系统中解出幂方程的指数，用于密码学
senses.example: The security of the protocol rests on how hard the discrete logarithm is to find.
senses.exampleCN: 这个协议的安全性取决于离散对数有多难求。
senses.why: cryptography took the ordinary logarithm and confined it to a finite system, where finding it becomes deliberately hard.
senses.whyCN: 密码学拿过普通对数，把它限制在有限系统中，找起来就变得刻意地困难。

senses.title: The complex logarithm
senses.definition: an extension of the logarithm to complex numbers, defined with an infinite family of values
senses.definitionCN: 把对数推广到复数，并用无穷多个值来定义
senses.example: The complex logarithm has infinitely many branches.
senses.exampleCN: 复对数有无限多个分支。
senses.why: extending the logarithm past zero forces a choice of branch, so the single value becomes a family.
senses.whyCN: 把对数越出零之外，就迫使人们选择分支，单个值于是变成一族值。

intro.en: Logarithm is a coined scientific term: Greek logos, here in the sense 'ratio', joined to arithmos 'number'. John Napier introduced it in 1614 to name the number that measures a ratio.
intro.cn: logarithm 是一个人造的科学术语：希腊语 logos 在此取「比」义，与 arithmos「数」结合。纳皮尔在 1614 年引入它，用来命名衡量比值的那个数。

items.en: Logos carried a wide range of meanings: word, account, reason and, in mathematics, ratio or proportion. The mathematical sense is the one used here.
items.cn: logos 的含义很广：言词、账目、理性，在数学里则指比或比例。这里用的是数学义。

items.en: Arithmos meant 'number'. Its earlier origin is not securely established, and any pre-Greek form offered for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: arithmos 意为「数」。它更早的来源没有可靠定论，凡为其给出的前希腊语形式都属重构。

items.en: John Napier combined the two Greek elements to mean a number measuring a ratio, and published the new word in his description of the logarithmic tables.
items.cn: 纳皮尔把这两个希腊构件合起来，指「衡量比值的数」，并在他介绍对数表的著作中公布了这一新词。

items.en: The coinage was Latinized as logarithmus and passed into the European languages through scholarly Latin.
items.cn: 这个新造词被拉丁化为 logarithmus，再经学术拉丁语传入欧洲各语言。

items.en: English adopted logarithm in the seventeenth century together with the tables, and the shorter form log followed in usage.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪随对数表一起接受了 logarithm，更短的 log 随后也在使用中出现。

items.en: The coining and its date are documented, but the deeper origin of arithmos is source uncertain; the commonly repeated pre-Greek etymology is a reconstruction rather than a proven derivation.
items.cn: 造词与年代有文献可查，但 arithmos 的更早来源不确定；常被转述的前希腊语词源是重构形式，并非已证实的派生。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds close to logarithm; the second group names the quantities and tools that sit beside it.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与 logarithm 相近；第二组是与它相邻的量与工具。

entries.definition: The adjective of logarithm; it describes scales and curves, not the number itself.
entries.definitionCN: logarithm 的形容词，描述刻度与曲线，而非那个数本身。

entries.definition: From Greek arithmetike 'the art of counting', built on the same arithmos 'number'; it names the subject, not a ratio-measuring number.
entries.definitionCN: 来自希腊 arithmetike「计数的技艺」，同样建立在 arithmos「数」上；它指这门学科，不是衡量比值的数。

entries.definition: From the name al-Khwarizmi through Medieval Latin; it looks like logarithm but has no Greek logos or arithmos inside.
entries.definitionCN: 经中世纪拉丁语来自花拉子米的名字；看似 logarithm，里面却没有希腊的 logos 或 arithmos。

entries.definition: From Greek logistikos 'skilled in calculation', but it developed separately to mean supply management and a growth model.
entries.definitionCN: 来自希腊 logistikos「精于计算」，但独立发展出后勤管理与一种增长模型的意思。

entries.definition: The number whose logarithm is given; it reverses the lookup rather than performing it.
entries.definitionCN: 指对数为某值的那个数；它把查表反过来，而非执行查表。

entries.definition: The power itself; a logarithm is that power asked as a question about a result.
entries.definitionCN: 指幂本身；对数则是把这个幂当作「要得到某结果」的问题来问。

entries.definition: The result of repeated multiplication; the logarithm names the count of repetitions.
entries.definitionCN: 指重复相乘的结果；对数命名的则是重复的次数。

entries.definition: A relation between two amounts; the 'ratio' inside logarithm names what the number measures, not a quotient itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指两个量之间的关系；logarithm 里的「比」说明这个数衡量什么，而不是指商本身。

entries.definition: A calculating tool that works by adding lengths proportional to logarithms.
entries.definitionCN: 一种计算工具，靠相加与对数成比例的长度来运算。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Greek pieces, the real family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的希腊构件、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: Greek logos 'ratio' plus arithmos 'number': a ratio-number, the number that measures a ratio.
normal.cn: 希腊 logos「比」加 arithmos「数」：比数，衡量比值的那个数。

normal.en: The family runs logarithm, logarithmic, logarithmically and antilogarithm.
normal.cn: 同族词有 logarithm、logarithmic、logarithmically 与 antilogarithm。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the bases: common logarithm, natural logarithm, binary logarithm.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出底数：常用对数、自然对数、二进制对数。

normal.en: The whole point is stated in one line: the log of a product is the sum of the logs.
normal.cn: 全部要点可以写成一行：积的对数等于对数的和。

normal.en: Before machines, people turned multiplication into addition and then read the answer off a table.
normal.cn: 在没有机器的年代，人们把乘法变成加法，再从表上读出答案。

abstract.en: Picture a staircase whose steps get shorter and shorter but never quite end.
abstract.cn: 想象一段楼梯，台阶越来越矮，却始终走不完。

abstract.en: Picture a giant compressed into a small box, still recognizable in outline.
abstract.cn: 想象一个巨人被压进小盒子，轮廓仍然认得出来。

abstract.en: Picture a question that asks not 'what is the answer' but 'how many times did you multiply'.
abstract.cn: 想象一个问题不问「答案是多少」，而问「你乘了几次」。

examples.en: The logarithm of a product equals the sum of the logarithms of its factors.
examples.cn: 积的对数等于各因子对数的和。

examples.en: Engineers once read logarithms from books the way we now read screens.
examples.cn: 工程师曾像我们今天读屏幕一样从书本上读对数。

examples.en: On a logarithmic scale the logarithm itself becomes the distance along the axis.
examples.cn: 在对数尺度上，对数本身就变成沿轴的这段距离。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「逻各」配「节奏」——按固定的「比例节奏」一层层数上去 → 对数

root: 希腊 logos（比、比例、言词）+ arithmos（数）→ 近代拉丁 logarithmus，纳皮尔 1614 年造词。arithmos 更早来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses all ask the same question in different settings: how many times must the base be multiplied? The answer is read from a definition, a base, a table, a law, a function, a cipher or a complex branch.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项在不同场合问同一个问题：底数要乘多少次？答案分别从定义、底数、数表、法则、函数、密码系统或复分支中读出。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an old table of columns, each column answering the question 'raised how many times'.
core.cn: 核心意象：一本旧数表排着纵列，每一列都在回答「要抬到几次」。

branches.en: THE QUESTION ITSELF: the exponent needed to reach a given number.
branches.cn: 问题本身：为得到某个给定数所需的幂。

branches.en: THE CHOICE OF BASE: ten for decimals, the natural constant for calculus, two for machines.
branches.cn: 底数的选择：十进制用十，微积分用自然常数，机器用二。

branches.en: THE OLD TOOL: a printed table and the law that turns products into sums.
branches.cn: 旧工具：印好的数表，以及把积化为和的法则。

branches.en: THE FUNCTION: the same value applied to every positive input.
branches.cn: 函数：把同一个值应用到每个正输入上。

branches.en: BEYOND ORDINARY NUMBERS: a deliberately hard exponent in ciphers, and an infinite family of branches in the complex plane.
branches.cn: 越出普通数之外：密码中刻意难求的指数，以及复平面上无穷多个分支。

intro.en: Logarithm is a modern coinage from two Greek nouns, so its building blocks are combining forms rather than inherited prefixes and suffixes.
intro.cn: logarithm 是由两个希腊名词合成的近代新词，因此它的构件其实是组合形式，而非继承下来的前缀与后缀。

latinIntro.en: The Greek elements logos and arithmos entered Latin as logos and arithmus; the coinage logarithmus is modern Latin, not classical.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊构件 logos 与 arithmos 以 logos、arithmus 的形式进入拉丁语；logarithmus 是近代拉丁造词，不属于古典拉丁。

items.exampleCN: 第一个构件贡献「比」这个意思。

items.example: The second element contributes the idea of number.
items.exampleCN: 第二个构件贡献「数」这个意思。

items.example: The logarithm measures how often the base is raised.
items.exampleCN: 对数衡量底数被抬了几次。

items.exampleCN: 这些数值按对数方式增长。

items.meaning: the number matching a given logarithm

items.exampleCN: 算术用的是同一个「数」构件。

items.meaning: logarithm in informal and technical use
items.example: The program takes the log of the input.

senses.example: She studied logic before turning to computer science.
senses.exampleCN: 她在转向计算机科学之前学过逻辑学。
senses.why: Greek logikē tekhnē was the 'art of reasoning', built on logos, 'word, reason, account'. The first sense is therefore the organized discipline that teaches how accounts must hang together.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 logikē tekhnē 是“推理之术”，建立在 logos“言词、理性、说明”之上。因此第一个义项就是教人如何让论述环环相扣的那门有组织的学科。

senses.title: The process: reasoning from premises
senses.definition: the process of drawing a conclusion from premises according to consistent rules
senses.definitionCN: 依照一致的规则从前提出发推出结论的过程
senses.example: The detective's logic led her to the only possible suspect.
senses.exampleCN: 侦探的推理把她引向唯一可能的嫌疑人。
senses.why: The discipline becomes an activity: a mind moves from what it accepts to what follows. The gears of the core image turn, and the conclusion is carried along whether one likes it or not.
senses.whyCN: 学科变成一种活动：心智从它接受的前提走向必然得出的结论。核心意象里的齿轮转动，结论不管人喜不喜欢都被带到终点。

senses.title: Sensible consistency: there is logic in it
senses.titleCN: 条理：事情说得通、前后一致
senses.definition: the quality of being sensible, consistent, or reasonable
senses.definitionCN: 明智、前后一致或合乎情理的性质
senses.example: There is a certain logic in her decision, even if I dislike it.
senses.exampleCN: 她的决定自有其道理，尽管我并不喜欢。
senses.why: When an account holds together, we say it has logic. The word moves from the formal rules to the everyday impression that nothing in the story contradicts anything else.
senses.whyCN: 当一个说法前后立得住，我们就说它有逻辑。这个词从形式规则转向日常印象：故事里没有任何一处与另一处相矛盾。

senses.title: Inner rationale: the logic of a situation
senses.titleCN: 内在道理：局势自身的运行逻辑
senses.definition: the underlying rationale that makes a situation, system, or institution work as it does
senses.definitionCN: 使某种局势、制度或体系如此运作的深层道理
senses.example: The logic of the market rewards speed over craftsmanship.
senses.exampleCN: 市场的逻辑奖励速度，而不是手艺。
senses.why: A system has its own forced sequence: given its rules, certain outcomes follow. Calling this its logic treats the system as an argument whose conclusion is already built in.
senses.whyCN: 一个体系有自己的强制序列：给定其规则，某些结果就会随之而来。把它称为“逻辑”，就是把该体系当作一个结论早已内置的论证。

senses.title: A formal system: Aristotelian, modal, fuzzy logic
senses.titleCN: 形式体系：亚里士多德逻辑、模态逻辑、模糊逻辑
senses.definition: a particular formal system of rules for valid inference, such as classical, modal, or fuzzy logic
senses.definitionCN: 某一套关于有效推理的形式规则体系，如经典逻辑、模态逻辑或模糊逻辑
senses.example: Modal logic adds rules for statements about necessity and possibility.
senses.exampleCN: 模态逻辑为关于必然性与可能性的陈述增加了规则。
senses.why: There is not one logic but many. Each system fixes its own symbols, axioms, and permitted moves, so 'a logic' names a game with explicit rules rather than reasoning in general.
senses.whyCN: 逻辑不止一套，而是有许多套。每个体系固定自己的符号、公理与允许的步骤，因此“一套逻辑”命名的是一场规则明确的游戏，而不是一般意义上的推理。

senses.title: Digital logic: gates and circuits
senses.titleCN: 数字逻辑：逻辑门与电路
senses.definition: the branch of electronics in which signals are combined by Boolean operations such as AND, OR, and NOT
senses.definitionCN: 电子学中用电平信号按与、或、非等布尔运算组合的分支
senses.example: The chip contains thousands of logic gates.
senses.exampleCN: 这块芯片包含数千个逻辑门。
senses.why: Formal rules become hardware: true and false turn into high and low voltage, and a gate output follows its inputs exactly as a conclusion follows premises. The abstract chain is now etched in silicon.
senses.whyCN: 形式规则变成硬件：真与假转为高电平与低电平，逻辑门的输出严格跟随输入，就像结论跟随前提。抽象的推理链此时被刻进硅片。

senses.title: Program logic: rules that decide behaviour
senses.titleCN: 程序逻辑：决定行为的规则
senses.definition: in computing, the set of rules in a program that determine how it responds to input
senses.definitionCN: 在计算机领域，程序中决定如何响应输入的一组规则
senses.example: The payment logic rejects cards with expired dates.
senses.exampleCN: 支付逻辑会拒绝过期日期的银行卡。
senses.why: Software encodes if-then structures: under condition A, do B. Business logic is the reasoning of an institution written as executable rules, so the same word covers both thought and machine.
senses.whyCN: 软件把“如果—那么”结构编码：在条件 A 下执行 B。业务逻辑就是把机构的推理写成可执行的规则，因此同一个词同时覆盖思维与机器。

senses.title: Argument structure: the chain from premise to conclusion
senses.titleCN: 论证结构：从前提到结论的链条
senses.definition: the structure of an argument, especially the relation between its premises and its conclusion
senses.definitionCN: 论证的结构，尤指前提与结论之间的关系
senses.example: The essay has a clear logic: each paragraph answers the objection raised before.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章逻辑清晰：每一段都回应前一段提出的反驳。
senses.why: Here logic is neither a discipline nor an inner rationale but the visible skeleton of a text. Each part must be held by the part before it, or the chain of proof breaks.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 logic 既不是学科，也不是内在道理，而是文本可见的骨架。每一部分都必须被前一部分扣住，否则证明链就断了。

senses.title: Usage boundary: countable only as a system
senses.titleCN: 用法边界：只有指“体系”时才可数
senses.definition: a usage limit: logic is usually uncountable; a logic or logics is used only for distinct formal systems, and logic is not a synonym for opinion or feeling
senses.definitionCN: 用法限制：logic 通常不可数；a logic 或 logics 只用于不同的形式体系，且 logic 不是 opinion 或 feeling 的同义词
senses.example: His anger is real, but it is not an argument in logic.
senses.exampleCN: 他的愤怒是真实的，但它在逻辑上不构成论据。
senses.why: The mass noun names reasoning as a substance, not a set of opinions. Counting begins only when separate rule-systems are compared. Emotion can motivate a claim, but it cannot supply the force of a conclusion.
senses.whyCN: 这个不可数名词把推理视作一种“质料”，而不是一堆观点。只有比较彼此独立的规则体系时才开始计数。情绪可以促使人提出主张，却不能提供结论的力量。

intro.en: Logic reaches English through Greek, Latin, and French. The chain logos to logikē to logica to logique is well documented; the Indo-European root *leg- is generally believed rather than certain.
intro.cn: logic 经由希腊语、拉丁语和法语进入英语。从 logos 到 logikē、logica、logique 的链条有清楚记载；其印欧词根 *leg- 只是一般认为，并非确定。

items.en: Greek logos meant 'word, speech, account, reason'. It could name a story told, an explanation given, or the rational order behind things.
items.cn: 希腊语 logos 意为“言词、言语、说明、理性”。它既可以指讲述的故事、给出的解释，也可以指事物背后的理性秩序。

items.en: Logos is generally traced to PIE *leg- 'to gather, pick up', specifically 'to pick words'. Speaking is pictured as gathering words and putting them in order; the deeper link is generally believed, not proved.
items.cn: logos 一般追溯到原始印欧语 *leg-“采集、拾起”，尤指“挑选词语”。说话被想象成把词语采集起来并排成次序；这一更深联系属于一般认为是，而非已经证明。

items.en: Logikē (tekhnē) meant the 'art of reasoning', the skill of using logoi well. Aristotle's works on argument turned that skill into a systematic study.
items.cn: logikē (tekhnē) 意为“推理之术”，即善用 logoi 的技能。亚里士多德关于论证的著作把这种技能变成了系统研究。

items.en: Latin logica and Old French logique carried the word westward. In the medieval curriculum logic was one of the three basic arts, alongside grammar and rhetoric.
items.cn: 拉丁语 logica 与古法语 logique 把这个词带到西方。在中世纪课程中，逻辑学与语法、修辞并列为三门基础技艺。

items.en: English logic appears in the 14c. Mathematical logic develops in the 19c., and digital logic in the 20c. gives the old art of reasoning a silicon body.
items.cn: 英语 logic 出现于 14 世纪。数理逻辑在 19 世纪发展起来，数字逻辑在 20 世纪给这门古老的推理之术装上了硅制的身体。

note.en: The first group shares the logos root or the log- shape; the second separates the discipline from reasoning, rationale, consistency, and one specific inference type.
note.cn: 第一组共享 logos 词根或 log- 词形；第二组把“逻辑学”与推理、根据、一致性以及一种具体推理类型分开。

entries.definition: following the rules of logic; sensible and consistent. It is the adjective built on logic.
entries.definitionCN: 符合逻辑规则的；有条理的。它是 logic 构成的形容词。

entries.definition: the organized movement and supply of goods and people. It comes from Greek logistikos 'skilled in calculating', also from logos.
entries.definitionCN: 货物与人员的有组织调运和供给。它来自希腊语 logistikos“擅长计算”，同样出自 logos。

entries.definition: a symbol or design used as a brand mark. It is shortened from logotype, from Greek logos 'word'.
entries.definitionCN: 用作品牌标记的符号或图案。它由 logotype 缩略而来，源自希腊语 logos“言词”。

entries.definition: the mental process of thinking things through. It is broader than logic and can include informal, practical thought.
entries.definitionCN: 把事情想通的思维过程。它比 logic 宽泛，可以包括非正式的、实践性的思考。

entries.definition: the reasons or explanation behind a decision or system. It names the content, not the formal study of inference.
entries.definitionCN: 某一决定或体系背后的理由或解释。它命名内容，而不是对推理的形式研究。

entries.definition: the property of parts fitting together without contradiction. It is one test of logic, not logic itself.
entries.definitionCN: 各部分彼此相容、不矛盾的性质。它是逻辑的一项检验，而不是逻辑本身。

entries.definition: inference from general premises to a necessary conclusion. It is one branch of logic, not the whole field.
entries.definitionCN: 从一般前提到必然结论的推理。它是逻辑学的一个分支，而不是整个领域。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: logos as word and reason, the real phrases formal logic and logic gate, and the everyday 'there is no logic in it'.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：作为言词与理性的 logos、真实短语 formal logic 与 logic gate，以及日常说法“毫无逻辑”。

normal.en: Logos meant 'word, account, reason'; logic is the art of making an account hold together.
normal.cn: logos 意为“言词、说明、理性”；logic 就是让一套说明站得住的技术。

normal.en: Formal logic writes the rules down: if the premises are true and the form is valid, the conclusion must be true.
normal.cn: formal logic 把规则写下来：如果前提为真且形式有效，结论必然为真。

normal.en: The logic of a situation is its inner forced sequence: given those rules, this outcome follows.
normal.cn: the logic of a situation 指局势内在的强制序列：给定那些规则，这个结果就会随之而来。

normal.en: A logic gate is the same reasoning in hardware: high and low inputs produce an output by rule.
normal.cn: 逻辑门是同一套推理的硬件版本：高、低输入按规则产生输出。

normal.en: Logical and illogical split the world into what follows and what contradicts itself.
normal.cn: logical 与 illogical 把世界分成两类：推得下去的，和自相矛盾的。

abstract.en: A chain of premises: each link is forced, and the last link cannot refuse the pull of the first.
abstract.cn: 一条前提链：每一环都是被迫的，最后一环无法拒绝第一环的拉力。

abstract.en: A transparent machine: put premises in at the top, and only the conclusion comes out at the bottom; emotion stays outside.
abstract.cn: 一台透明的机器：前提从上方放入，只有结论从下方出来；情绪留在机器之外。

abstract.en: A skeleton that holds an argument upright: remove one bone and the whole body of proof collapses.
abstract.cn: 一副撑起论证的骨架：抽掉一根骨头，整个证明的身体就塌了。

examples.en: The argument is elegant, but its logic is flawed at the second step.
examples.cn: 这个论证很漂亮，但它的逻辑在第二步就有漏洞。

examples.en: There is a simple logic to her method: test the cheapest fix first.
examples.cn: 她的方法有一个简单的内在道理：先试最便宜的修法。

examples.en: Modern processors are built from millions of logic gates.
examples.cn: 现代处理器由数百万个逻辑门构成。

dict_mnemonic.text: “老季克”——老季讲话条理清楚，句句都推得下去 → logic 逻辑

root: 希腊语 logos“言词、理性、说明”，经 logikē tekhnē“推理之术”而来；核心是“用有章法的言词把道理讲通”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of logic, all from logos as ordered speech: the discipline, the act of reasoning, the feel of consistency, the rationale inside a system, a formal rule-system, silicon gates, program rules, the skeleton of an argument, and the boundary of countable uses.
sensesIntro.cn: logic 的九个义项都出自 logos 作为“有秩序的言词”：学科、推理行为、前后一致的感觉、体系内的道理、形式规则体系、硅片上的门、程序规则、论证骨架，以及可数用法的边界。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: ordered words lock together and force a conclusion.
core.cn: 核心意象：有次序的言词彼此咬合，迫使结论出现。

branches.en: THE DISCIPLINE AND ITS SYSTEMS: logic is both the study of valid form and the named formal systems it compares.
branches.cn: 学科及其体系：logic 既是对有效形式的研究，也是它所比较的各套具名形式体系。

branches.en: THE ACT AND THE SKELETON: reasoning moves from premise to conclusion, and the written argument shows that chain.
branches.cn: 行为与骨架：推理从前提到结论，书面论证则展示这条链。

branches.en: CONSISTENCY AND RATIONALE: an account holds together, and a system carries its own forced logic.
branches.cn: 一致性与内在道理：一套说明前后立得住，一个体系则带有自身强制的逻辑。

branches.en: MACHINES: Boolean gates and program rules turn inference into hardware and code.
branches.cn: 机器：布尔门与程序规则把推理变成硬件与代码。

branches.en: BOUNDARY: logic is mass-noun reasoning, countable only when separate systems are meant.
branches.cn: 边界：logic 是不可数的推理，只有指彼此独立的体系时才可数。

intro.en: Logic is a Greek-derived noun ending in -ic. English builds the adjective with -al, the adverb with -ally, the person with -ian, and the negative with il-.
intro.cn: logic 是源自希腊语、以 -ic 结尾的名词。英语用 -al 构成形容词，用 -ally 构成副词，用 -ian 构成人物名词，用 il- 构成否定。

latinIntro.en: The family rests on Greek logos 'word, reason'. Dialogue, monologue, logistics and analogy all contain that same second element or its derivative.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词族建立在希腊语 logos“言词、理性”上。dialogue、monologue、logistics、analogy 都含有同一词素或其派生形式。

items.meaning: following the rules of logic; sensible
items.meaningCN: 逻辑的；合乎逻辑的（-al 表示“与……有关”）
items.example: That is the logical conclusion from the evidence.
items.exampleCN: 那是从证据得出的合乎逻辑的结论。

items.meaning: in a way that follows from the premises
items.meaningCN: 逻辑上；合乎逻辑地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: Logically, the second claim depends on the first.
items.exampleCN: 从逻辑上说，第二个主张依赖于第一个。

items.meaning: a person who studies or works with logic
items.meaningCN: 逻辑学家（-ian 表示从事该学科的人）
items.example: The logician rewrote the proof in symbols.
items.exampleCN: 这位逻辑学家用符号重写了证明。

items.meaning: not following from the premises; inconsistent
items.meaningCN: 不合逻辑的；缺乏条理的（il- 表示否定）
items.example: It is illogical to expect a different result from the same input.
items.exampleCN: 指望同样的输入产生不同的结果是不合逻辑的。

items.example: The noun is the source of logic and of -logy.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是 logic 与 -logy 的来源。

items.example: The stem appears in dialogue, catalogue and logic.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干见于 dialogue、catalogue 与 logic。

items.example: It shapes logical, the adjective built on logic.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 logical 这一形容词。

items.example: The ending marks logic as a discipline, logike in Greek.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把 logic 标为一门学问，希腊语作 logike。

items.meaning: a formal argument from two premises
items.example: The syllogism is the oldest tool of formal logic.
items.exampleCN: 三段论是形式逻辑最古老的工具。

latinEntries.meaning: a conversation between two or more people
latinEntries.meaningCN: 对话；对白（dia- 表示“之间”，logos 表示“言词”）

latinEntries.meaning: a long speech by one person
latinEntries.meaningCN: 独白；长篇独语（mono- 表示“单一”）

latinEntries.meaning: the organized supply and movement of goods and people
latinEntries.meaningCN: 物流；后勤（源自“擅长计算”，与 logos 同族）

latinEntries.meaning: a comparison based on a shared relation
latinEntries.meaningCN: 类比；类推（按相同的比例或关系作比较）

definition_en: the angular distance of a place east or west of a prime meridian, or, in older use, length
core_image: 地球仪上一圈圈从北极到南极的竖线，把表面切成一条条东西的瓣
scene: 航海者在船舱里把当地时间与格林尼治时间对照。A navigator compares local noon with Greenwich time to find the longitude.
sceneCN: 这里 longitude 指「某地相对本初子午线的东西角距离」（第 1 个义项：以本初子午线为零度、按角度量出的东西位置）；句意为航海者把当地正午与格林尼治时间对照，从而求出经度。图中可辨识物件：航海钟、海图、六分仪、地球仪。

senses.title: Angular distance from the prime meridian
senses.titleCN: 经度：相对本初子午线的东西角距离
senses.definition: the angular distance of a place east or west of a fixed prime meridian, measured in degrees
senses.definitionCN: 某地相对一条固定本初子午线向东或向西的角距离，以度数计
senses.example: The observatory stands at a longitude of seventy degrees west.
senses.exampleCN: 这座天文台位于西经七十度。
senses.why: Latin longitudo meant 'length'; on the globe the east-west length of the known world became an angle measured from a chosen meridian.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 longitudo 意为「长度」；在地球上，已知世界的东西「长度」变成了从选定子午线量起的角度。

senses.title: A meridian or line of longitude
senses.definition: a great circle passing through both poles, drawn on a map to mark a longitude
senses.definitionCN: 过南北两极、在地图上标出某经度的大圆
senses.example: The captain marked the line of longitude on the chart.
senses.exampleCN: 船长在海图上标出了那条经线。
senses.why: The drawn line is the visible form of the measured angle, so the same word names coordinate, line and position.
senses.whyCN: 画出的线是所测角度的可见形态，因此同一个词兼指坐标、线与位置。

senses.title: Position east or west of a reference
senses.titleCN: 经度位置：位于参考线以东或以西
senses.definition: the east-west position of a place relative to a reference meridian
senses.definitionCN: 某地相对参考子午线的东西位置
senses.example: Ships approaching the coast reported their longitude every hour.
senses.exampleCN: 接近海岸的船只每小时报告一次经度位置。
senses.why: Navigation treats longitude as a place on a scale from west to east, not only as a degree value.
senses.whyCN: 航海把经度当作从西到东的刻度上的位置，而不只是度数。

senses.title: Length, archaic
senses.titleCN: 长度：事物的长向尺寸（古义）
senses.definition: the length of a thing, the original Latin sense, now obsolete in everyday use
senses.definitionCN: 事物的长度，即拉丁本义，今日常用语中已废弃
senses.example: The old geometry text speaks of the longitude of a rectangle.
senses.exampleCN: 那本旧几何书谈到矩形的长度。
senses.why: This is the literal Latin sense; it survives only in historical and technical writing after geography took the word over.
senses.whyCN: 这是拉丁本义；在地理义占据该词之后，只残存于历史与技术文字中。

senses.title: Celestial longitude
senses.titleCN: 黄经：天体沿黄道量出的角度
senses.definition: the angular distance of a celestial body measured eastward along the ecliptic
senses.definitionCN: 天体沿黄道向东量出的角距离
senses.example: Ephemeris tables list the celestial longitude of the moon.
senses.exampleCN: 星历表列出月球的黄经。
senses.why: The sky was mapped with the same length-turned-angle logic, using the ecliptic as its zero circle.
senses.whyCN: 天空也按同一套「长度转为角度」的逻辑绘制，只是零度圈改用黄道。

senses.title: Longitude and time
senses.titleCN: 经度与时差：经度差对应的时间差
senses.definition: the fixed relation between a difference in longitude and a difference in local time
senses.definitionCN: 经度差与当地时间差之间的固定关系
senses.example: Every fifteen degrees of longitude equals one hour of time.
senses.exampleCN: 每十五度经度相当于一小时的时间差。
senses.why: Because the earth turns at a steady rate, an east-west angle can be converted into a time difference, which made the chronometer method possible.
senses.whyCN: 地球匀速自转，东西向的角度可换算成时间差，这正是航海钟测经法的基础。

senses.title: Difference of longitude
senses.titleCN: 经度差：两地经线之间的角度
senses.definition: the angle between the meridians of two places, used in navigation and surveying
senses.definitionCN: 两地经线之间的夹角，用于航海与测量
senses.example: The survey first computed the difference of longitude between the two towns.
senses.exampleCN: 测量队先算出两镇之间的经度差。
senses.why: Two positions are compared by subtracting their longitudes, so the word also names the gap rather than a single coordinate.
senses.whyCN: 比较两地位置要相减经度，因此这个词也指这段差值而非单一坐标。

senses.title: Geodetic versus astronomical longitude
senses.titleCN: 大地经度与天文经度：两种测定口径
senses.definition: the east-west coordinate defined either by a reference ellipsoid or by the local vertical
senses.definitionCN: 分别以参考椭球或当地铅垂线定义的东西坐标
senses.example: Geodetic longitude differs slightly from astronomical longitude.
senses.exampleCN: 大地经度与天文经度略有差异。
senses.why: Precise mapping distinguishes a coordinate on the ellipsoid from one fixed by gravity, so longitude splits into two technical readings.
senses.whyCN: 精密制图把椭球面上的坐标与由重力确定的坐标分开，经度因此分为两种技术读数。

intro.en: Longitude comes from Latin longitudo 'length', built on longus 'long'. Geography narrowed 'length' to the east-west span of the world and then to an angle. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: longitude 来自拉丁 longitudo「长度」，由 longus「长的」构成；地理学把「长度」收窄为世界的东西跨度，再收窄为角度。年代均为约数。

items.en: Longus meant 'long'; its Indo-European source is reconstructed as a form meaning 'long', so the deeper form is a reconstruction rather than a recorded word.
items.cn: longus 意为「长的」；其印欧语来源被重构为表示「长」的形式，因此更深层的词形属重构而非有记录的词。

items.en: Longus plus -tudo gave longitudo, 'length, extent'.
items.cn: longus 加 -tudo 构成 longitudo，意为「长度、幅度」。

items.en: In sixteenth-century geography the 'length' of the known world was fixed as the east-west angular distance from a prime meridian.
items.cn: 16 世纪地理学把已知世界的「长度」定为相对本初子午线的东西角距离。

items.en: Celestial longitude applies the same measure to the sky, counting eastward along the ecliptic.
items.cn: 黄经把同一量度用于天空，沿黄道向东计数。

items.en: From the seventeenth to the eighteenth century the practical need to fix longitude at sea drove chronometer astronomy and precision timekeeping.
items.cn: 17 至 18 世纪，在海上确定经度的实际需要推动了航海钟天文学与精密计时。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dates only): the archaic 'length' sense faded without a recorded final use, and the first maritime applications are not precisely dated. The root is secure.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代）：古义「长度」在无记录的情况下淡出，最早的航海应用亦无确切年代。词根本身可靠。

note.en: Group one holds the -tude words that share spelling patterns with longitude; group two holds the map and sky terms it is paired with or confused with.
note.cn: 第一组是与 longitude 共享拼写模式的 -tude 词；第二组是常与它配对或混淆的地图与天球术语。

entries.definition: From latus 'broad': the north-south angle, drawn as east-west parallels.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 latus「宽」：南北向角度，画成东西走向的纬线。

entries.definition: From altus 'high': height above a reference, with no east-west meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 altus「高」：高出基准的高度，与东西位置无关。

entries.definition: From magnus 'great': the size or brightness of something, especially a star.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 magnus「大」：某物的大小或亮度，尤指恒星。

entries.definition: From aptus 'fit': a natural capacity for learning, with no geographic use.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 aptus「合适」：学习的天赋，不含地理用法。

entries.definition: A great circle through the poles; a meridian is one specific line of longitude, often the reference line.
entries.definitionCN: 过两极的大圆；经线是某一条具体的经度线，常指参考线。

entries.definition: A circle parallel to the equator; it is the drawn form of a latitude, not a longitude.
entries.definitionCN: 与赤道平行的圈；它是纬度的画线形态，不是经度。

entries.definition: The direction of one point from another, measured as an angle from north; it answers 'which way', not 'how far east'.
entries.definitionCN: 一点相对另一点的方向，从正北量角；它回答「朝哪边」，而非「向东多远」。

entries.definition: Either of the numbers that fix a position; latitude and longitude are the two geographic coordinates.
entries.definitionCN: 用于确定位置的两个数之一；纬度与经度就是两个地理坐标。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Latin 'length', real map practice and the real history of the longitude problem.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁「长度」、真实的地图实践与真实的经度难题史。

normal.en: Longus 'long' + -tudo 'state': the world's east-west length, later measured as an angle.
normal.cn: longus「长」+ -tudo「状态」：世界的东西长度，后来被量成角度。

normal.en: Longitude lines run north-south and measure east-west position; latitude lines do the reverse.
normal.cn: 经线南北走向，却量东西位置；纬线正好相反。

normal.en: Fifteen degrees of longitude correspond to one hour of solar time.
normal.cn: 十五度经度对应一小时的太阳时。

normal.en: The prime meridian at Greenwich is the zero line for longitude.
normal.cn: 格林尼治本初子午线是经度的零度线。

normal.en: The 'longitude problem' was solved by accurate clocks at sea, not by better maps alone.
normal.cn: 「经度难题」是靠海上精确计时解决的，仅靠更好的地图不够。

abstract.en: Picture a clock and a globe joined by a single shaft, so time turns into distance.
abstract.cn: 想象一只钟与一个地球仪由一根轴连在一起，时间由此变成距离。

abstract.en: Picture an orange cut into wedges from top to bottom rather than around its middle.
abstract.cn: 想象一只橙子从上到下切成瓣，而不是横着切。

abstract.en: Picture a ruler laid north-south while it measures how far east you are.
abstract.cn: 想象一把尺南北摆放，却量出你向东走了多远。

examples.cn: 这座小镇位于东经一百度。

examples.en: Difference in longitude can be converted into difference in local time.
examples.cn: 经度差可以换算成地方时差。

examples.en: Early sailors could find latitude but not longitude.
examples.cn: 早期的水手能测纬度，却测不出经度。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all come from 'length' turned into a coordinate: the east-west angle, the line that marks it, the position it names, the older literal length, the sky's version, the time it implies, the gap between two places, and the two ways surveyors define it.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都来自「长度」被转为坐标：东西向角度、标出它的经线、它所命名的位置、更早的字面长度、天空中的对应量、它对应的时间、两地之间的差值，以及测量者定义它的两种口径。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line running pole to pole, marking how far east or west a place has moved from a zero line.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条从极到极的线，标出某地相对零度线向东或向西移动了多远。

branches.en: COORDINATE AND PLACE: a degree value and the position it picks out are two faces of one coordinate.
branches.cn: 坐标与位置：度数与它所标出的位置，是同一坐标的两面。

branches.en: LINE AND GAP: one meridian marks a place, two meridians measure the distance between places.
branches.cn: 线与差：一条经线标记地点，两条经线量出地点间的距离。

branches.en: OLD LENGTH: the literal Latin sense survives as a technical term for extent.
branches.cn: 旧义长度：拉丁本义作为表示幅度的技术词留存。

branches.en: SKY: the same measure is counted eastward along the ecliptic.
branches.cn: 天空：同一量度沿黄道向东计数。

branches.en: TIME AND DATUM: longitude converts into time, and into two technical readings on ellipsoid or plumb line.
branches.cn: 时间与基准：经度可换算为时间，也可分成椭球面与铅垂线的两种技术读数。

intro.en: Longitude is built on Latin longus 'long' and a state suffix; the same root runs through long, elongate and elongation.
intro.cn: longitude 由拉丁 longus「长的」与状态后缀构成；同一词根贯穿 long、elongate 与 elongation。

latinIntro.en: Latin longus 'long' yields longitude, longitudinal and prolong; the verb elongare 'to lengthen' gives elongate and elongation.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 longus「长」衍生 longitude、longitudinal 与 prolong；动词 elongare「使变长」衍生 elongate 与 elongation。

senses.title: Running along the long axis: from one end to the other
senses.titleCN: 沿长轴：从这一头走到那一头
senses.definition: placed or measured along the longest dimension of an object, from one end to the other
senses.definitionCN: 沿物体最长的那一维、从一端到另一端放置或测量的
senses.example: The tunnel was drilled longitudinally through the ridge.
senses.exampleCN: 隧道顺着山脊的走向纵向钻通。
senses.why: Latin longitudo is longus 'long' plus -tudo, the suffix that turns a quality into a measurable extent. Adding -alis makes a direction adjective: the direction that follows that extent.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 longitudo 是 longus「长的」加 -tudo，这个后缀把性质变成可度量的延展。再加 -alis 就成了方向形容词：顺着那段延展走的方向。

senses.title: Of length as a dimension, not width or height
senses.titleCN: 长度的：作为一个维度而言
senses.definition: relating to length as a measured dimension rather than to width, breadth or height
senses.definitionCN: 指长度这一可测量的维度，而不是宽、阔或高
senses.example: Longitudinal measurement showed that the beam had grown two centimetres.
senses.exampleCN: 长度测量显示这根梁长了两厘米。
senses.why: The Latin noun named plain 'length' long before it named a line on the globe. The adjective keeps that older sense of a dimension, so any measure taken along the long side is longitudinal.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁名词先指朴素的「长度」，很久以后才指地球上的经线。形容词保留了这一较早的维度义，因此凡是沿长边量出的尺寸都叫 longitudinal。

senses.title: Cut lengthwise: the longitudinal section
senses.titleCN: 纵切：把物体顺着长度剖开
senses.definition: made by cutting along the length of a body, so that the cut surface shows its internal parts from end to end
senses.definitionCN: 沿物体的长度剖开而制成的切面，切口从一端贯通到另一端，露出内部构造
senses.example: The anatomist drew a longitudinal section of the stem.
senses.exampleCN: 解剖学家画出了茎的纵切面。
senses.why: In anatomy and engineering a cut is named by the axis it follows. Down the long axis gives a longitudinal section; across it gives a transverse one, and the pair of words defines each other.
senses.whyCN: 在解剖学与工程里，切面按它顺着的那根轴命名。顺着长轴切就是纵切面，横着切就是横切面，这两个词互相定义。

senses.title: Longitudinal wave: vibration along the line of travel
senses.titleCN: 纵波：振动方向与传播方向在同一条线上
senses.definition: of a wave in which the particles move back and forth along the same line in which the wave itself travels
senses.definitionCN: 指波中质点沿着波传播的同一条线来回振动的
senses.example: Sound in air is a longitudinal wave; light is a transverse one.
senses.exampleCN: 空气中的声波是纵波，光是横波。
senses.why: Here the contrast is with transverse. The push travels down a row of touching balls, and each ball moves along the same line as the push, so the whole disturbance is longitudinal.
senses.whyCN: 这里与横波相对。推力沿一排相触的球传下去，每颗球都沿推力的同一条线运动，整个扰动因此是纵向的。

senses.title: Longitudinal study: following the same people through time
senses.titleCN: 纵向研究：把同一批人一路跟下去
senses.definition: of research that follows the same subjects over a long period and measures change as it happens
senses.definitionCN: 指长期追踪同一批研究对象、随时记录其变化的
senses.example: The longitudinal study tracked the children from age five to thirty.
senses.exampleCN: 这项纵向研究追踪这些孩子从五岁一直到三十岁。
senses.why: The dimension of length moved from space into time. A study that runs the full length of years is longitudinal; one that slices across the population at a single moment is cross-sectional.
senses.whyCN: 长度这一维度从空间挪到了时间上。跑满若干年长度的是纵向研究；只在一个时刻横切人群的是横向研究。

senses.title: Longitudinal data and comparison: one group against itself
senses.titleCN: 纵向数据与比较：同一群体与自己比
senses.definition: of records or comparisons that set the same group against its own earlier or later state
senses.definitionCN: 指把同一群体与其先前或后来的状态作对照的记录或比较
senses.example: Longitudinal data let researchers separate age effects from generation effects.
senses.exampleCN: 纵向数据让研究者把年龄效应与代际效应区分开。
senses.why: Once a study runs along time, its records become a line of successive points. Comparing along that line, rather than across people, is what makes the comparison longitudinal.
senses.whyCN: 研究一旦沿时间展开，记录就成了一条由连续时点连成的线。沿这条线比较，而不是在人与人之间横比，才使这种比较成为纵向的。

senses.title: Of longitude: position measured east and west
senses.titleCN: 经度的：东西方向上的位置
senses.definition: relating to longitude, the east-west position measured in degrees, or to the lines that mark it
senses.definitionCN: 指经度——以度数计的东西向位置——或指标示经度的那些线
senses.example: The ship's longitudinal position was fixed at twenty degrees west.
senses.exampleCN: 这艘船的经度位置定在西经二十度。
senses.why: Longitudo also named the 'length' of the known world measured east to west. That usage fixed longitude as the terrestrial coordinate, and the adjective followed the noun into geography.
senses.whyCN: longitudo 也曾指已知世界东西方向的「长度」。这一用法把 longitude 固定为地理坐标，形容词也随之进入地理学。

senses.title: Along the chain: levels of command or stages of supply
senses.titleCN: 沿链条：层级上下或产业链前后
senses.definition: of links that run between levels of a hierarchy or between successive stages of a supply chain
senses.definitionCN: 指贯穿等级各层之间、或产业链各连续环节之间的连接
senses.example: Analysts describe links from supplier to customer as longitudinal ties within the industry.
senses.exampleCN: 分析者把从供应商到客户的连接称为产业内的纵向联系。
senses.why: Here the length is the chain itself: the axis runs from raw material to end user, or from head office down through the levels. A link along that axis is longitudinal rather than lateral.
senses.whyCN: 这里的「长度」就是链条本身：轴从原料走到最终用户，或从总部往下穿过各层级。顺着这根轴的连接就是纵向的，而不是横向的。

intro.en: Longitudinal comes from Late Latin longitudinalis, an adjective built on Latin longitudo 'length'. Longitudo is longus 'long' plus -tudo, the suffix that turns a quality of size into a noun of extent. English borrowed the adjective in the 14th century for what runs lengthwise; its use for studies that follow people over years belongs to the 20th century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: longitudinal 出自晚期拉丁语 longitudinalis，是加在拉丁语 longitudo「长度」上的形容词。longitudo 由 longus「长的」加 -tudo 构成，这个后缀把尺寸性质变成表示延展的名词。英语在 14 世纪借入该形容词，指顺着长度方向的；用于长期追踪人的研究则是 20 世纪的事。年代为大致估计。

items.en: Longitudinal study becomes a settled term in psychology and medicine for research that follows the same subjects across years.
items.cn: longitudinal study（纵向研究）在心理学与医学中成为固定术语，指跨年份追踪同一批对象的研究。

items.en: Physics and anatomy standardise longitudinal wave and longitudinal section as the contrast pair to transverse.
items.cn: 物理学与解剖学把 longitudinal wave（纵波）与 longitudinal section（纵剖面）固定下来，作为与 transverse（横切）相对的一对术语。

items.en: English longitudinal is first recorded, borrowed from Late Latin longitudinalis, describing what lies or runs lengthwise.
items.cn: 英语 longitudinal 首次见于记载，借自晚期拉丁语 longitudinalis，描述顺着长度放置或延伸的东西。

items.en: Latin longitudo 'length' is longus 'long' plus -tudo; the same noun also names east-west distance on the globe, which gives longitude.
items.cn: 拉丁语 longitudo「长度」由 longus「长的」加 -tudo 构成；同一个名词也指地球上东西向的距离，由此产生 longitude。

items.en: longus goes back to the reconstructed root *dlonghos 'long', which also yields English long and German lang; the asterisk marks a reconstructed, unattested form.
items.cn: longus 可追溯到重构形式 *dlonghos「长的」，这一形式也产生英语 long 与德语 lang；星号表示重构而未见记载的形式。

note.en: The first group separates words that merely look similar from those that truly share the root; the second compares words that overlap only part of the meaning.
note.cn: 第一组把只是长得像的词与真正同源的词分开；第二组比较只共享部分含义的词。

entries.definition: relating to latitude, the north-south position. It is built on latus 'side, broad', not on longus 'long', so the two look like a pair but come from different roots.
entries.definitionCN: 指纬度，即南北方向的位置。它建立在 latus「侧面、宽」上，而不是 longus「长」，因此两词看似成对，来源却不同。

entries.definition: the east-west coordinate, and the noun from which longitudinal is built. It keeps the older sense of 'length' inside a geographic term.
entries.definitionCN: 东西向坐标，也是 longitudinal 所由构成的名词。它在地理术语内部保留了较早的「长度」义。

entries.definition: a deep desire. It comes from Old English langian 'to grow long for', a native verb about the mind stretching out, and not from Latin longus.
entries.definitionCN: 深切的渴望。它出自古英语 langian「因思念而心长」，是描述心思被拉长的本族动词，并非来自拉丁语 longus。

entries.definition: describing a study that measures many different people at one moment. It contrasts with longitudinal, which measures the same people at many moments.
entries.definitionCN: 指在同一时刻测量许多不同人的研究。它与纵向研究相对：后者是在许多时刻测量同一批人。

entries.definition: following one after another in order. It names the order of events, while longitudinal names the axis along which they are followed.
entries.definitionCN: 按次序一个接一个。它说的是事件先后顺序，而 longitudinal 说的是顺着哪根轴去追踪。

entries.definition: lasting or extending over a long period. It stresses duration alone; longitudinal stresses that measurements run along that duration.
entries.definitionCN: 持续或延伸很长时间。它只强调时长，而 longitudinal 强调测量是沿着这段时间展开的。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real pieces of the word and its real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想只使用这个词真实的构成成分和真实同族词，不用编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: longus 'long' plus -tudo gives longitude 'length'; add -alis and you get the adjective of direction along that length.
normal.cn: longus「长」加 -tudo 得到 longitude「长度」；再加 -alis 就得到「顺着这个长度」的方向形容词。

normal.en: The -i- before -tudinal is a linking vowel, not a plural marker; do not read longitudinal as 'longitudes'.
normal.cn: tudinal 前的那个 -i- 是连接元音，不是复数标记；不要把它读成 longitude 的复数。

normal.en: The same longus yields longevity, where long life is literally a 'long age', and oblong, where ob- 'towards' plus longus means 'longer than broad'.
normal.cn: 同一个 longus 还产生 longevity（字面「长的年岁」即长寿）和 oblong（ob-「朝向」加 longus，意为「比宽更长」）。

normal.en: Longitude and longitudinal are the same family; the noun names the coordinate, the adjective names the direction along it.
normal.cn: longitude 与 longitudinal 同属一族；名词指坐标，形容词指沿该坐标的方向。

normal.en: Transverse is the built-in opposite: transverse cuts across the axis, longitudinal runs along it.
normal.cn: transverse（横切）是它内在的对立面：横切是切过轴线，纵向是顺着轴线。

abstract.en: See one thread pulled from end to end of a spool; everything called longitudinal is measured along that thread.
abstract.cn: 想象从线轴的一端到另一端拉出一根线；所有叫 longitudinal 的东西都是沿这根线量的。

abstract.en: Let the thread turn into time: a longitudinal study is the same thread running through years rather than across people.
abstract.cn: 把这根线换成时间：纵向研究就是同一根线穿过许多年份，而不是横过许多人。

abstract.en: The word always asks one question: is the measurement along the long line, or across it?
abstract.cn: 这个词总在问同一个问题：这个测量是顺着长线，还是横穿过去？

examples.en: The engineers took longitudinal measurements before cutting the pipe.
examples.cn: 工程师在切割管道前先做了纵向测量。

examples.en: A longitudinal study can show how reading habits change with age.
examples.cn: 纵向研究能显示阅读习惯如何随年龄改变。

examples.en: The drill followed a longitudinal path through the rock.
examples.cn: 钻头沿着一条纵向路径穿过岩层。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「龙脊丢头」——顺着龙脊一路走到底，方向始终不变 → longitudinal 纵向的、沿长轴的

root: 拉丁语 longus「长的」＋-tudo（延展名词后缀）→ longitudo「长度、经度」＋-alis（形容词后缀）→ longitudinal。核心是「顺着最长的那一维走到底」，再由空间延伸到时间与链条。

sensesIntro.en: All eight senses keep one image: a line drawn from one end of a thing to the other. What changes is what the line is drawn through: a beam, a cut surface, a sound wave, a set of years, a table of records, the globe, or a chain of command.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都保留同一个意象：从物体一端拉到另一端的一条线。变化的只是这条线穿过什么：梁、剖面、声波、一串年份、一张记录表、地球，还是一条指挥链。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one line drawn from end to end along the longest side of a thing.
core.cn: 核心意象：沿物体最长的一边，从一端到另一端画出的一条线。

branches.en: LONG AXIS: the line is spatial, and any measure taken along it is a length measure.
branches.cn: 长轴：这条线在空间里，沿它量出的任何尺寸都是长度尺寸。

branches.en: CUT LENGTHWISE: the knife follows the line, so the exposed face shows the inside from end to end.
branches.cn: 纵切：刀顺着这条线走，露出的面就从一端到另一端展示内部。

branches.en: WAVE ALONG THE LINE: in a longitudinal wave the vibration itself moves along the same line as the wave.
branches.cn: 线上之波：纵波里振动本身就沿着与波相同的那条线移动。

branches.en: TIME AS LENGTH: the line becomes a run of years, and records along it form longitudinal data.
branches.cn: 时间成线：这条线变成一串年份，沿线的记录就构成纵向数据。

branches.en: CHAIN AS LENGTH: geography uses the east-west line, organisations use the line from top level to bottom or from supplier to buyer.
branches.cn: 链条成线：地理学用东西向的线，组织则用从顶层到底层、或从供应商到买方的线。

intro.en: Longitudinal is Latin long- plus -itudo plus -alis. The suffix -tudo (English -tude) makes a noun of extent from an adjective, and -alis (English -al) makes a relating adjective from that noun.
intro.cn: longitudinal 是拉丁词干 long- 加 -itudo 再加 -alis。后缀 -tudo（英语 -tude）把形容词变成表示延展的名词，-alis（英语 -al）再把该名词变成关系形容词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin pieces are longus 'long' and the two suffixes -tudo and -alis. longus also underlies longitude, longevity and oblong.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁成分是 longus「长的」以及 -tudo、-alis 两个后缀。longus 还支撑着 longitude、longevity、oblong。

items.meaning: relating to length or running lengthwise
items.meaningCN: 与长度有关的；顺长度方向的
items.example: The beam was measured along its longitudinal axis.
items.exampleCN: 这根梁沿它的长轴被测量。

items.meaning: length, and later the east-west coordinate
items.example: The island lies at fifteen degrees of longitude.
items.exampleCN: 这座岛位于经度十五度。

items.meaning: in the direction of the length
items.example: The wood was cut longitudinally.
items.exampleCN: 这块木头是纵向切开的。

items.structure: longus (long), with the native English form
items.meaning: measuring a great distance from end to end
items.meaningCN: 长的；长的（英语本族同源形式）
items.example: A long table filled the room.

items.structure: Old English lengþu, the native noun matching Latin longitudo
items.meaning: the measure of something from end to end
items.meaningCN: 长度（英语本族名词，与拉丁 longitudo 对应）
items.example: Measure the length of the wall first.

items.meaningCN: 拉长；使延长（e- 表示向外）
items.example: The cells elongate as they divide.

items.meaning: the act of stretching out, or the amount stretched
items.example: The test measures the elongation of the wire.
items.exampleCN: 这项测试测量金属丝的伸长量。

items.meaning: long life, great length of years
items.meaningCN: 长寿；长久的寿命（字面「长的年岁」）
items.example: Diet affects human longevity.
She placed an oblong tray on the table.
items.exampleCN: 她把一个长条形的托盘放在桌上。

items.structure: longitudo, the same noun used as a technical coordinate
items.meaning: distance east or west of a standard meridian
items.meaningCN: 相对标准子午线的东西向距离；经度
items.example: Sailors needed accurate clocks to find longitude.
items.exampleCN: 水手需要准确的钟表来确定经度。

latinEntries.meaning: forms a noun of extent or quality, as in longitude
latinEntries.meaningCN: 构成表示延展或性质的名词，如 longitude
长度；也指东西向的延展

latinEntries.meaning: relating to, of the kind of

definition_zh: 环；圈；扣环；循环；回路；环路；绕行
definition_en: a shape in which a line or rope curves back and crosses or nearly crosses itself, a ring used for fastening, a repeated cycle in a process or program, or the act of moving around something in a curve
core_image: 一段绳子被绕成圆圈，两头几乎相接，像刚打好的一个结
scene: 雨后的山路上，车灯照着前方一个弯回来的岔口。The road loops around the hill before joining the highway.
sceneCN: 这里 loop 是「绕行、环行」（第 5 个义项：沿弧线绕过某物）；句意为这条路绕过山丘之后才接上公路。图中可辨识物件：山路、车灯、弯回来的岔口。

pos.zh: 环；圈；扣环；循环；回路；环路

derivatives.zh: 由 loop 加 -y 构成，义为「古怪的；脑子绕不清的」
由 loop 加 -ing 构成，义为「成环；循环往复」
由 loop 与 back 复合，义为「回环；环回路径」
由 loop 与 hole 复合，原指墙上留出的窄孔，后指「漏洞」

senses.title: A curve that closes on itself
senses.definition: a shape made when a rope, wire or line curves round and crosses or nearly crosses itself
senses.definitionCN: 绳子、金属丝或线条弯回来、彼此交叉或几乎交叉时形成的形状
senses.example: She made a loop with the rope and hung it on the hook.
senses.exampleCN: 她用绳子打了个环，挂在钩子上。
senses.why: A line bent back on itself leaves the eye with a closed figure; the shape, not the material, is what the word first names.
senses.whyCN: 一条线弯回自身，在眼里留下一个闭合的图形；这个词最先命名的不是材料，而是这个形状。

senses.title: A ring used for fastening
senses.definition: a small ring or curved strip fixed to something so that a belt, hook or cord can pass through it
senses.definitionCN: 固定在物体上的小环或弧形条，用来让腰带、钩子或绳索引穿过去
senses.example: The belt goes through a leather loop at the waist.
senses.exampleCN: 腰带从腰间的一个皮环里穿过去。
senses.why: Once a rope's closed curve can hold another thing, the same outline can be sewn or moulded onto an object; the ring stays because it still does the holding.
senses.whyCN: 一根绳子的闭合曲线一旦能套住别的东西，同样的轮廓就可以缝上或铸在物件上；环之所以留下，是因为它仍在承担「套住」这件事。

senses.title: A repeated cycle in a process or program
senses.definition: a set of instructions or events that returns to its starting point and repeats, especially in computing
senses.definitionCN: 一组回到起点并不断重复的指令或事件，尤用于计算机领域
senses.example: The program got stuck in a loop and printed the same line forever.
senses.exampleCN: 程序卡在循环里，一直打印同一行。
senses.why: A closed curve has no exit; when the steps of a process follow one another back to the start, the path of that process looks like the curve, so the repeat borrows the name.
senses.whyCN: 闭合的曲线没有出口；当一个过程的步骤依次回到起点，这个过程走过的路径就像那条曲线，于是重复也借用了这个名字。

senses.title: To form a curve or ring
senses.definition: to make something into a curve that closes on itself, or to be shaped in that way
senses.definitionCN: 把某物弄成闭合的曲线，或本身以那种形状存在
senses.example: Loop the cable twice around the frame before tightening it.
senses.exampleCN: 把缆线在架子上绕两圈再拉紧。
senses.why: The noun names the closed shape; the verb turns that shape into an action and asks what the hands are doing to the material.
senses.whyCN: 名词命名的是闭合的形状；动词把这个形状变成动作，问的是双手正在对材料做什么。

senses.title: To move around something in a curve
senses.definition: to travel in a curve that goes round something and often comes back towards the starting side
senses.definitionCN: 沿着一条绕过某物、常常又回到出发一侧的曲线行进
senses.example: The path loops around the pond and returns to the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 这条小路绕过池塘，又回到门口。
senses.why: A traveller going round a hill traces the same closed line on the ground, so the name of the shape becomes a verb for the route.
senses.whyCN: 绕山而行的人在土地上画出的正是同一条闭合线，于是形状的名字变成了路线上的动词。

intro.en: Loop is first recorded in Middle English for a bend in a rope; where the word came from is still debated, and the modern technical senses grew out of that rope ring.
intro.cn: loop 最早见于中古英语，指绳子上的一处弯折；它的来源至今仍有争论，现代的技术义项都是从那个绳环生长出来的。

items.en: The earliest recorded loop names a bend or fold in a rope or cord, not yet a perfect circle.
items.cn: 最早记录的 loop 指绳子或细索上的一个弯折，还不一定是完整的圆。

items.en: One common suggestion links it to Old Norse hlaup, a leap, through the running knot that a pulled rope forms; another points to Middle Dutch loopen, to run. Neither is certain.
items.cn: 一种常见说法认为它与古诺斯语 hlaup（跳跃）有关，因为拉紧的活结会形成环；另一种说法指向中古荷兰语 loopen（奔跑）。两说都不确定。

items.en: By the sixteenth century loop covered any ring-shaped curve, including loops of ribbon, metal and lace.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，loop 已泛指任何环状曲线，包括丝带、金属和花边形成的圈。

items.en: Railways and telegraphy gave loop a closed route or circuit, as in a loop line that turns back on itself.
items.cn: 铁路与电报事业给 loop 添上「闭合路线、回路」的义项，如折返回原处的环线。

items.en: Computing made the repeated instruction cycle a loop, and sound and video added the sense of playing a passage over and over.
items.cn: 计算机把反复执行的指令周期叫作 loop，声音与影像又添上「反复播放一段内容」的义项。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms and compounds built on loop; the near-meaning group gathers words for rings, coils and repeated cycles.
note.cn: 形近组收由 loop 构成的变形与复合词；近义组收表示环、盘绕与循环的词。

entries.definition: Silly or slightly crazy, as if one's thoughts have gone round in circles.
entries.definitionCN: 由 loop 加 -y 构成，义为「古怪的；脑子像绕成圈一样糊涂的」。

entries.definition: The act of forming a loop, or a repeated replay of a passage.

entries.definition: A path or signal that returns to its own source.
entries.definitionCN: 由 loop 与 back 复合，义为「回环；环回路径」。

entries.definition: A round shape or circular object, especially one with an open centre.
entries.definitionCN: 环；圆圈；强调圆形本身，不一定有交叉或回环。

entries.definition: A length of wire or rope wound into a series of circles.
entries.definitionCN: 盘绕的一圈；强调材料被螺旋状连续卷起。

entries.definition: A set of events that repeats in the same order.
entries.definitionCN: 循环；周期；强调事件按同样顺序重复，不强调形状。

entries.definition: A closed route that starts and ends at the same place, or a path for electric current.
entries.definitionCN: 闭合路线；电路；强调起点与终点相接的一整圈。

normalIntro.en: The word is anchored in a rope bent back into a ring, and its family keeps returning to circles, repeats and routes that come back.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词锚定在一根弯回成环的绳子上，它的同族词反复回到圆圈、重复以及折返回来的路线。

normal.en: Two o letters in the middle of loop look like two joined rings, which is exactly the shape the word names.
normal.cn: loop 中间的两个字母 o 像两个相连的圆圈，正好是这个单词所指的形状。

normal.en: In the loop means inside a circle of people who know something; out of the loop means left outside that circle.
normal.cn: in the loop 指在知道内情的圈子里；out of the loop 指被留在圈子外面。

normal.en: A computer loop repeats the same instructions until a condition stops it, because a closed path keeps returning to where it began.
normal.cn: 计算机的 loop 会反复执行同样的指令直到条件终止，因为闭合的路径总是回到起点。

normal.en: Loop back is what a road or a signal does when it turns round and comes back towards its source.
normal.cn: loop back 就是道路或信号折返、朝源头回来时所做的动作。

normal.en: Loopy adds -y to loop: thoughts that go round and round without reaching a clear end sound slightly mad.
normal.cn: loopy 在 loop 后加 -y：想法一圈圈绕却到不了清楚的终点，听起来就有点古怪。

abstract.en: A loop has no obvious exit; walking it once only brings you back to the same gate.
abstract.cn: 一个环没有明显的出口；走一圈只会把你带回同一扇门。

abstract.en: A circle of information works the same way: those inside hear everything, those outside hear nothing.
abstract.cn: 信息的圈子也是一样：圈内的人什么都听得到，圈外的人什么都听不到。

abstract.en: Habits are loops too, which is why breaking one means cutting the path rather than walking it faster.
abstract.cn: 习惯也是环，所以改掉一个习惯要切断路径，而不是走得更快。

examples.en: The road loops around the hill before joining the highway.
examples.cn: 这条路绕过山丘之后才接上公路。

examples.en: The program got stuck in a loop and printed the same line forever.
examples.cn: 程序卡在循环里，一直打印同一行。

examples.en: She made a loop with the rope and hung it on the hook.
examples.cn: 她用绳子打了个环，挂在钩子上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「卢普」——绳子一绕就圈成个环；loop 就是环、圈，也指循环。

root: 中古英语 loop 最早指绳子上的弯折；词源一般认为与古诺斯语 hlaup（跳跃）或中古荷兰语 loopen（奔跑）有关，但两说都无定论；现代又引申出循环、环线、回路等义。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a line that bends back into a ring; the senses divide into the shape, the fastening ring, the repeated cycle, the act of forming a loop, and the act of travelling round.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一条弯回成环的线；义项由此分出形状本身、起固定作用的环、反复的循环、把东西弄成环的动作，以及绕行一圈的动作。

definition_zh: 松的；不紧的；宽松的；不受约束的；不严谨的；释放
definition_en: not firmly fixed or tied, not fitting closely, free from control or restraint, not strict or precise, or to set something free
core_image: 一根原本绷紧的绳子忽然松下来，绳结松垮地垂在木桩边
scene: 清晨的码头上，一条小船的缆绳在桩上松了半圈，船身轻轻晃动。The rope came loose during the night and the boat drifted a little.
sceneCN: 这里 loose 是「松的、不紧的」（第 1 个义项：没有牢牢固定）；句意为夜里缆绳松了，船稍微漂开。图中可辨识物件：码头、缆绳、木桩、小船。

pos.zh: 松的；不紧的；宽松的；不受约束的；不严谨的

collocations.zh: 未了结的细节；松散的线头

senses.title: Not firmly fixed or tied
senses.definition: not held tightly in place, so that it can move, slip or come off
senses.definitionCN: 没有被牢牢固定在原位，因此会移动、滑动或脱落
senses.example: One of the screws is loose and the shelf wobbles.
senses.exampleCN: 有一颗螺丝松了，架子摇摇晃晃。
senses.why: The core image is tension gone slack: what should grip no longer grips, so the first sense names anything that can move because it is not held fast.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是张力消失、变松：本该咬住的不再咬住，所以第一个义项指任何因为没被牢牢固定而能移动的东西。

senses.title: Not fitting closely
senses.definition: of clothes or coverings, larger than the body so that it does not press against it
senses.definitionCN: 指衣服或覆盖物比身体大，不会紧贴身体
senses.example: He wore a loose shirt to the interview.
senses.exampleCN: 他穿着一件宽松的衬衫去面试。
senses.why: When cloth stops pressing on the body, the same slackness that lets a screw slip lets air move under a garment; the sense moves from fastening to fit.
senses.whyCN: 当布料不再压住身体，让螺丝滑动的那种松弛便让空气能在衣服下面流动；义项从「固定」转到「合身程度」。

senses.title: Free from control or restraint
senses.definition: not kept in a cage, prison or strict system, and able to move or act freely
senses.definitionCN: 没有被关在笼子、监狱或严格体系里，能够自由移动或行动
senses.example: The gate was left open and the dog got loose.
senses.exampleCN: 大门没关，狗跑了出去。
senses.why: A thing not tied down is also not controlled; once the physical rope is gone, the word can describe anyone or anything escaping restraint.
senses.whyCN: 没有被捆住的东西也不受控制；一旦具体的绳子消失，这个词就能形容任何摆脱约束的人或物。

senses.title: Not strict or precise
senses.definition: of language, rules or thinking, not exact and allowing more than one interpretation
senses.definitionCN: 指语言、规则或思考不精确，允许不止一种解释
senses.example: The article gives only a loose definition of the term.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章只给这个术语下了一个宽泛的定义。
senses.why: A tight knot leaves no room to move; a statement that leaves room to move is felt to be tied just as loosely, so precision becomes the thing that is not fastened down.
senses.whyCN: 系紧的结不留活动的余地；一句留有余地的话也被觉得系得同样松，于是精确性成了那个没被固定住的东西。

senses.title: To set free or let go
senses.definition: to release an animal, a person or a held object, or to fire an arrow or shot
senses.definitionCN: 放开动物、人或握住的物体，也可指射出箭或子弹
senses.example: The keeper loosed the dogs at sunset.
senses.exampleCN: 日落后，看守人把狗放开了。
senses.why: The adjective describes the state of being untied; the verb is the act that produces that state, so the same word becomes the hand opening.
senses.whyCN: 形容词描述的是「已被解开」的状态；动词则是产生这种状态的动作，于是同一个词变成了张开的手。

intro.en: Loose is generally traced to a Germanic adjective for slackness and freedom; English later built loosely, loosen and looseness on it.
intro.cn: loose 一般认为源自一个表示松弛与自由的日耳曼语形容词；英语后来在它之上构成了 loosely、loosen 与 looseness。

items.en: The adjective is generally traced to Old Norse lauss, meaning loose, free or dissolute, which entered English during the Norse settlements.
items.cn: 这个形容词一般认为源自古诺斯语 lauss，意为松的、自由的、放纵的，在诺斯人定居时期进入英语。

items.en: The reconstructed Germanic form means loose or free; German los and Dutch los are close relatives, and the English suffix -less grows from the same family.
items.cn: 重构的日耳曼语形式意为松的、自由的；德语 los 与荷兰语 los 是近亲，英语后缀 -less 也出自同一词族。

items.en: Middle English loose appears as an adjective for what is not bound, and a verb meaning to set free grows beside it.
items.cn: 中古英语的 loose 已是形容词，指没有被捆住的东西；旁边又长出表示「释放」的动词。

items.en: The word spreads from ropes and cages to clothes, morals and language, giving phrases such as loose woman and loose translation.
items.cn: 这个词从绳索与笼子扩展到衣服、品行与语言，产生 loose woman 与 loose translation 之类的说法。

items.en: Modern English keeps the physical and abstract senses side by side and builds the family loosely, loosen and looseness; it is a different word from lose, which means to misplace or be deprived of.
items.cn: 现代英语让具体的与抽象的义项并排存在，并构成 loosely、loosen、looseness 等同族词；它与表示「丢失、失去」的 lose 是不同的词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers family forms and the easily confused lose; the near-meaning group gathers words for slackness, loose fit and freedom.
note.cn: 形近组收同族形式以及容易混淆的 lose；近义组收表示松弛、宽松与自由的词。

normalIntro.en: The word is anchored in a Germanic adjective for slackness and freedom, and its family keeps returning to things that are not held tight.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词锚定在一个表示松弛与自由的日耳曼语形容词上，同族词反复回到没有被紧紧固定住的东西。

normal.en: Loose starts in Old Norse lauss, a word for free as well as slack; the physical and the social senses were there from the beginning.
normal.cn: loose 源自古诺斯语 lauss，这个词既指松弛也指自由；具体的与社会的义项从一开始就都在。

normal.en: The suffix -less comes from the same Germanic family, which is why less and loose both carry the idea of being without.
normal.cn: -less 这个后缀出自同一日耳曼词族，所以 less 与 loose 都带着「没有、缺少」的意思。

normal.en: Loosen adds -en to loose and means to make less tight; loosely adds -ly and describes the manner.
normal.cn: loosen 在 loose 后加 -en，表示「使变松」；loosely 加 -ly，描述做事的方式。

normal.en: Loose change is coins carried loose in a pocket, not fastened into a wallet or roll.
normal.cn: loose change 是散放在口袋里、没有捆进钱包或纸卷的零钱。

normal.en: Do not confuse loose with lose: loose is slack, lose is to no longer have something.
normal.cn: 不要把 loose 与 lose 弄混：loose 是松，lose 是失去某物。

abstract.en: A knot that has gone slack can still look tied, which is why loose rules and loose talk are hard to notice at first.
abstract.cn: 松掉的结看上去仍像系着，所以宽松的规则与随意的言辞起初不容易被察觉。

abstract.en: Freedom and slackness share one word because both mean that nothing is holding you in place.
abstract.cn: 自由与松弛共用一个词，因为两者都意味着没有东西把你固定住。

abstract.en: A loose end is not a failure; it is simply a thread the story has not tied yet.
abstract.cn: 松着的线头不是失败，它只是故事还没系上的一根线。

scene: 长途航班落地后，人们拖着行李走进安静的休息区，有人直接把自己放进最软的那张沙发里。We sank into the soft chairs of the airport lounge and finally relaxed.
sceneCN: 这里 lounge 是名词「休息室、候机厅」（第 4 个义项：供等候休息的公共房间）；句意为我们陷进机场休息室的软椅，终于放松下来。画面里可认出休息区、行李和沙发。

senses.title: To sit or lie in a relaxed, lazy way
senses.definition: to sit, lean or lie somewhere in a comfortable and lazy way
senses.definitionCN: 以舒服而懒散的姿势坐、靠或躺在某处
senses.example: He lounged on the sofa all afternoon with the television on.
senses.exampleCN: 他整个下午都懒洋洋地靠在沙发上，开着电视。
senses.why: The word was first used of slow, languid movement, so the core image of sinking comfortably into a seat naturally becomes the verb for lazy resting.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最早描写缓慢而慵懒的动作，核心意象是舒服地陷进座位，由此自然长出表示懒散休息的动词义。

senses.title: To stand or move about in an idle way
senses.titleCN: 懒散地闲逛；无所事事地消磨时间
senses.definition: to spend time in a place standing, leaning or walking about without any purpose
senses.definitionCN: 在某个地方站着、倚着或随便走走，没有明确目的，消磨时间
senses.example: A few young men lounged by the gate, waiting for nothing in particular.
senses.exampleCN: 几个年轻人懒散地倚在大门边，也不特意等什么。
senses.why: If the body is too relaxed to act with purpose, resting in a seat widens into drifting about a place, so the same lazy posture gives the idle sense.
senses.whyCN: 当身体懒散到没有行动目标时，坐着休息就扩展成在某个地方闲荡，同一副慵懒姿态便衍生出无所事事的意思。

senses.title: A comfortable sitting room in a house
senses.definition: a room in a house where people sit and relax, especially in British English
senses.definitionCN: 住宅里供人坐下休息的房间，尤见于英式英语
senses.example: The family watched the match together in the lounge.
senses.exampleCN: 一家人在客厅里一起看比赛。
senses.why: The room got its name from what people do there: since to lounge is to relax lazily, the room set aside for lounging became the lounge.
senses.whyCN: 这个房间因人们在那里的动作而得名：既然 lounge 是懒散地休息，专门用来休息的房间就成了 the lounge。

senses.title: A comfortable room for waiting in a public place
senses.definition: a comfortable room at an airport, station, hotel or club where people can wait or relax
senses.definitionCN: 机场、车站、旅馆或俱乐部里供人等候、放松的舒适房间
senses.example: They waited for their flight in the business lounge.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在商务候机厅里等航班。
senses.why: Waiting used to be done standing in a hall; giving waiters a soft room where they can lounge comfortably extends the home sense to public buildings.
senses.whyCN: 过去人们等候时只能站在大厅里；给等候者一间可以懒散放松的软房间，就把家庭义延伸到了公共建筑里。

senses.title: A room or bar for drinking and socialising
senses.definition: a room in a hotel, club or bar, often with music, where people drink and talk
senses.definitionCN: 旅馆、俱乐部或酒吧里常配音乐的房间，供人喝酒、聊天
senses.example: The band played quiet jazz in the cocktail lounge.
senses.exampleCN: 乐队在鸡尾酒廊里演奏轻柔的爵士乐。
senses.why: A room built for relaxing attracts drinks and conversation, so the waiting room sense drifts to the room where lounging happens over a drink.
senses.whyCN: 为放松而设的房间自然引来酒和聊天，于是等候室的意思偏向了那间一边喝一杯一边懒散度过的房间。

senses.title: A man's ordinary business suit
senses.definition: a man's usual matching jacket and trousers for business or formal daywear, in lounge suit
senses.definitionCN: lounge suit 里指男士平常穿的上衣西裤成套西服，用于商务或白天的正式场合
senses.example: The invitation asked gentlemen to wear a lounge suit.
senses.exampleCN: 请柬要求男士穿普通西服出席。
senses.why: Because a suit worn loosely at home was once contrasted with stiffer formal dress, the lazy word came to mark everyday formality rather than ease.
senses.whyCN: 由于在家松散穿用的西服曾与拘谨的礼服相对，这个表示懒散的词转而标记日常的正式装束，而不是指舒适本身。

senses.title: A man who idles in social places to impress others
senses.titleCN: 游手好闲的社交客（lounge lizard，旧式戏谑）
senses.definition: in the old informal phrase lounge lizard, a man who spends his time in lounges and hotels trying to impress people
senses.definitionCN: 旧式非正式说法 lounge lizard 里指常泡休息室与旅馆、装腔作势讨人喜欢的男人
senses.example: In the old novel, a lounge lizard occupied the hotel bar every evening.
senses.exampleCN: 在那本旧小说里，一个游手好闲的社交客每晚都占着旅馆酒吧。
senses.why: A person who only lounges about becomes a fixed type, so the lazy verb combines with a comic image to name the idle social climber.
senses.whyCN: 只会闲荡的人固化为一种人物类型，表示懒散的动词与滑稽意象组合，就用来称呼无所事事的社交客。

senses.title: Soft, relaxed popular music
senses.titleCN: 轻音乐风格的 lounge music
senses.definition: in lounge music, a style of quiet, easy-listening popular music played in bars and lounges
senses.definitionCN: lounge music 里指酒吧、酒廊常放的舒缓、放松的轻音乐风格
senses.example: The cafe plays lounge music all afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 这家咖啡馆整个下午都放着轻音乐。
senses.why: The music takes its name from the place and mood it fits, so the room for lounging lends its name to sound made for lounging.
senses.whyCN: 这种音乐因适合的场所和心情而得名，供人懒散休息的房间便把名字借给了为懒散而作的声音。

intro.en: The origin of lounge is uncertain; it first appears in sixteenth-century English as a verb for lazy, slow movement, and several explanations compete.
intro.cn: lounge 的来源不确定；它最早见于十六世纪英语，作动词表示缓慢慵懒的动作，目前并存几种解释。

items.en: The verb lounge appears in the sixteenth century meaning to move or act lazily and slowly; no earlier ancestor is securely recorded.
items.cn: 动词 lounge 在十六世纪出现，意为懒散、缓慢地行动；没有可靠的更早祖先形式被记录下来。

items.en: A common suggestion links it to the older word lungis, meaning a slow, lazy person; this connection is generally held but not proven.
items.cn: 一种常见看法把它与更早的 lungis（慢性子、懒人）联系起来；这一关联被普遍接受但未获证实。

items.en: Some treat lounge as an expressive or imitative coinage for languid movement, like several other lazy-motion verbs; this remains a hypothesis.
items.cn: 也有人认为 lounge 是表达慵懒动作的拟声性造词，与其他几个表示懒散动作的动词相仿；这仍只是假说。

items.en: From the lazy action came a place where one lounges: by the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries the noun named a place to lounge, and later a room for it.
items.cn: 由懒散动作引申出可以懒散的场所：十六至十七世纪名词开始指可供闲躺的地方，后来指专门的房间。

items.en: Modern English keeps both sides: the verb for lazy resting and wandering, and the noun for sitting rooms, airport lounges, bars and soft music.
items.cn: 现代英语保留了两个方向：动词表示懒散休息与闲荡，名词表示客厅、机场候机厅、酒吧与轻音乐风格。

normal.en: The lounger is the person who lounges or the chair they lie on.

abstract.en: The word pictures a body that has nowhere to be, so time itself feels soft.
abstract.cn: 这个词描绘一副无处可去、任由时间变得柔软的身体。

abstract.en: Rooms that host laziness borrow the name of the laziness, like the sofa lending its comfort to the room.
abstract.cn: 容纳慵懒的房间借走了慵懒的名字，仿佛沙发的舒适被搬进了房间。

abstract.en: Lounge holds both the verb of rest and the noun of place, joining action and setting in one sound.
